title: Digitization and digital transformation
context: Evaluate the following statements on the concept of digitization and digital transformation:
statements: Digitization primarily means the use of digital information and communication technology in concrete processes, not merely owning devices.
Digital transformation describes the change that this use triggers in the economy, administration and the private sphere — for example in processes, customer contact or offerings.
Anyone who equates digitization and digital transformation is naming the same process twice and needs no distinction between application and the resulting change.
Technology can simultaneously shift internal process control, customer relationships and the design of products and services.
As soon as servers and laptops have been purchased, digital transformation is considered complete, even if processes and offerings remain unchanged.
tactical_explanations:
Application is at the centre, not the inventory list. Digitization means the use of digital information and communication technology: systems control, data flow, work steps are supported. A computer or cash register alone without use in processes does not meet the term.

The statement is true.

Change follows application. Digital transformation is the restructuring that the use of digital technology drives in parts of the economy, administration and the private sphere. Process control, customer contact and the offering can shift; buying devices alone is not yet transformation.

The statement is true.

Two coupled terms, not a pair of synonyms. Digitization names the application of digital technology; digital transformation names the change that this application triggers. Anyone who swaps the two words without a difference in meaning mixes tool and effect.

The statement is false.

Doing business changes in several places. Technology affects how companies control internal processes, how they stay in contact with customers and how they design products and services and bring them to market. Later the same effects are assigned to the dimensions backstage, frontstage and digitized result.

The statement is true.

Hardware alone does not complete the transformation. Digital transformation means change through the application of digital technology. Mere acquisition without a change in processes or offerings does not meet this standard; technology without noticeable restructuring remains application without transformation.

The statement is false.

title: Technology in the company
context: Evaluate the following statements on what the use of technology changes in companies:
statements: Technology can influence how companies control internal processes in order to operate as efficiently as possible.
Customer contact and taking requirements into account remain largely untouched by technology; changes mainly affect warehouse accounting.
The design and market introduction of products and services can also change through technology.
For such shifts, the words digitization or digital transformation are often used.
Technology mainly affects communication with suppliers; product and service design remain practically untouched by it.
tactical_explanations:
Efficiency behind the scenes is a central field of impact. Companies control internal processes to operate as efficiently as possible, and technology changes exactly this control: work steps are supported, automated or reordered.

The statement is true.

Customer contact is by no means untouched by technology. Technology changes how companies stay in touch with customers and take their requirements and needs into account. Later this same outward side is called frontstage. Limiting the effect to warehouse accounting cuts out this core field.

The statement is false.

The market side belongs in the picture of change. Products and services are designed and brought to market, and that too can shift through technology: new forms, new channels, new timing. Digitization is therefore not only an internal process topic.

The statement is true.

The two words are used precisely for these shifts. When technology changes processes, customer relationships and the market offering, people often speak of digitization or digital transformation. The wording is tied to observable change.

The statement is true.

Product and service design are not left out. Technology also affects how offerings are shaped and brought to market. Narrowing the effect to supplier communication cuts out this field of impact and is too narrow.

The statement is false.

title: Three dimensions of digitization
context: Evaluate the following statements on the three dimensions of digitization:
statements: In a company context, digital opportunities for change can be ordered along three dimensions.
The first dimension concerns business processes behind the scenes (backstage).
The second dimension, the frontstage, means the connection between customers and the company.
The third dimension is aimed mainly at internal accounting and leaves products and services aside.
Companies may concentrate on exactly one dimension only; parallel work on several dimensions is not envisaged.
tactical_explanations:
Three dimensions form the organising grid: processes behind the scenes, the connection to the customer and digitization of the result. The point is starting points in the business, not an endless list of arbitrary technology topics.

The statement is true.

Backstage carries the first dimension. Business processes behind the scenes support value creation and are increasingly extended and controlled by systems. The internal focus lies on the economic use of resources.

The statement is true.

Frontstage means the outward side toward the customer. The second dimension is understood as the connection between customers and the company and is the external focus. Orientation around the customer and designing offerings with users in mind belong here.

The statement is true.

Result of value creation, not internal accounting alone. The third dimension deals with how the result of value creation can be extended through technology — that is, with the digitization of products and services. Accounting alone does not hit this dimension.

The statement is false.

One or more dimensions are allowed. Companies can deliberately concentrate on one or more of the three dimensions and derive a digitization strategy from that. The claim that only exactly one dimension is allowed is too narrow.

The statement is false.

title: Backstage and value creation
context: Evaluate the following statements on the first dimension of digitization:
statements: A company's internal focus lies on the economic use of resources in order to create products and services from them.
In doing so, value is to be created; one then speaks of value creation.
Business processes behind the scenes support value creation and are increasingly extended and controlled by systems.
If work steps are digitally supported, a digitally supported business process emerges.
Backstage denotes the public customer interface; processes behind the scenes fall under frontstage.
tactical_explanations:
Resources are converted internally into goods and services. The internal focus lies on the economic use of resources to create products and services. That is the behind-the-scenes side of the company, not the shop window toward the customer.

The statement is true.

Value creation is the other name for the same process. Value is to be created; put differently, value creation takes place. Value arises here in the process behind the scenes, supported by business processes.

The statement is true.

Processes carry value creation and are extended by systems. Business processes behind the scenes support value creation and are increasingly extended and controlled by systems. Digital support means extending and steering the flow behind the stage.

The statement is true.

Digitally supported business process is the fitting expression. If work steps can be digitally supported, exactly this construct emerges. Technology supports the steps but does not replace the concept of the process.

The statement is true.

Behind the scenes and the stage are swapped. Backstage means behind the scenes: internal business processes that support value creation. The public connection to the customer is the frontstage. Anyone who reads backstage as the customer connection mixes the first two dimensions.

The statement is false.

title: What a business process is
context: Evaluate the following statements on the definition of a business process:
statements: A business process is a complex workflow of several logically connected activities.
This workflow contributes (value) for the company toward a business objective.
Business processes can be carried out repeatedly.
A business process may have only exactly one defined end; alternative endings of the same workflow are not allowed.
A business process includes a clearly defined start and one or more defined ends.
tactical_explanations:
Complex and logically connected: that is the structure. A business process is not a single hand movement but a workflow of several activities that hang together logically. Anyone who reduces the term to an isolated activity misses the definition.

The statement is true.

Value toward a goal is a required element. The workflow contributes value for the company toward a business objective. A random jumble of activities without a goal reference would therefore not be a business process.

The statement is true.

Repeatability belongs to it. Business processes can be carried out repeatedly: purchasing, order handling or similar patterns are not meant as a one-off event but as a workflow that can start again.

The statement is true.

Several ends are envisaged, not forbidden. The definition names a clearly defined start and one or more defined ends. Pickup and shipping can, for example, be two clear endings of the same order process.

The statement is false.

Start and one or more ends belong to the definition. Besides the clearly defined start, one or more defined ends are envisaged. Having several ends does not contradict clarity.

The statement is true.

title: Documentation and process model
context: Evaluate the following statements on documenting business processes:
statements: Recording a process through a digital system — documentation — helps employees communicate the process.
Within such a process, different people can keep an overview and make decisions more purposefully.
A visual representation, also called a process model, can give new employees a first overview of a central workflow, for example in purchasing.
Process documentation only makes sense on paper; digital systems are hardly suitable for it because workflows change too quickly.
Process models mainly serve top management; interns do not need them because they learn the workflow on site anyway.
tactical_explanations:
Documentation makes the workflow communicable. If a process is recorded digitally, employees can explain and pass it on more easily. Without such recording, knowledge often sticks with individual people.

The statement is true.

Overview and decision-making hang together. Within a digitally supported process, different people keep an overview and can make relevant decisions faster and more purposefully.

The statement is true.

A process model is the visual representation. Such a model can help grasp a central process — for example in purchasing — quickly, especially when someone is new to the company.

The statement is true.

Digital systems are expressly envisaged for documentation. Recording through a digital system is part of the description; limiting it to paper contradicts the purpose of digital process support.

The statement is false.

Not only top management. Process models serve orientation in the company, including new employees and interns. Reserving them for leadership locks out the actual users.

The statement is false.

title: Order at the bookseller
context: Evaluate the following statements on the example of a digital business process at a bookseller such as Thalia:
statements: For an online order at a bookseller such as Thalia, steps are triggered in the background immediately so that the product can be made available quickly.
An internal system summarises the order and notifies the next available employee for the further steps.
Detail steps can include: retrieving the warehouse location, selecting the product and preparing the order for pickup or shipping.
The order process already ends once the order is recorded in the internal system — delivery or readiness for pickup are then only a side matter.
After successful processing, the employee marks the order in the system and can turn to the next order.
tactical_explanations:
Background steps start immediately. An online order triggers internal work so that the product reaches the customer as quickly as possible. The click in the shop is the start, not yet fulfilment.

The statement is true.

System and notification interlock. The order is summarised internally and assigned to an available employee who takes on the detail steps.

The statement is true.

Detail steps are concrete. Warehouse location, product selection and preparation for pickup or shipping belong to the typical flow behind the scenes.

The statement is true.

Recording is not the end. The process ends with delivery or readiness for pickup. Anyone who declares it finished with the system entry confuses the start of processing with fulfilment toward the customer.

The statement is false.

A completion mark frees the path. After successful processing the order is closed in the system; the employee can turn to the next case. That belongs to the repeatable character of the process.

The statement is true.

title: Frontstage and customers
context: Evaluate the following statements on the second dimension of digitization:
statements: The frontstage is understood as the connection between customers and the company and forms the external focus.
Depending on the setting, a private person, a company or a public institution can count as a customer.
Digitization on the frontstage is limited to providing printed catalogues as PDFs; more targeted consideration of user wishes is not meant.
Requirements and needs of users and offerings oriented toward the customer are in the foreground.
Digitization opens up potential to take user wishes into account more efficiently and more purposefully.
tactical_explanations:
Frontstage is the outward side. Connection to the customer and external focus belong together; warehouse control alone does not cover this dimension.

The statement is true.

Three possible customers appear in the list. Private person, company or public institution — offerings oriented toward the customer must handle this variety.

The statement is true.

PDF catalogues alone fall short. Frontstage aims at offerings oriented toward the customer and at more efficient, more purposeful consideration of user wishes. Mere file formats without a better view of requirements do not hit the dimension.

The statement is false.

User wishes are in the foreground. Designing offerings oriented toward the customer and orientation toward requirements and needs are the core of the frontstage.

The statement is true.

New potential is expressly named. Digitization is meant to take users' wishes on board more efficiently and more purposefully — not only to mirror existing catalogues digitally.

The statement is true.

title: Foot scanner in shoe retail
context: Evaluate the following statements on the example of the shoe fashion chain Humanic:
statements: When buying shoes online or in a store, fit — size, width and similar questions — remains a central challenge.
Humanic has introduced an in-store and smartphone-app service that records users' requirements via a 3D foot scanner.
The scanner creates a 3D image of the feet and stores it online in the customer account.
The foot-scanner service is aimed mainly at wholesalers; end customers hardly use it in the setting described.
In store and for the next online order, the digital footprint can be matched against the desired shoe model.
tactical_explanations:
Fit remains the core question. Size, cut and width cost time and nerves — online and in store. That is exactly where the service described starts.

The statement is true.

Service in store and via app. Humanic records user wishes with a 3D foot scanner and stores them digitally — an example of frontstage potential.

The statement is true.

Image and account belong together. The 3D image of the feet lands online in the customer account and is available for later matching.

The statement is true.

The target group is end customers buying shoes, in store and via app — not wholesale. Narrowing it to wholesalers misses the example.

The statement is false.

Matching against the model. The digital footprint helps check the optimal fit for the desired shoe in store and online.

The statement is true.

title: Smart products and services
context: Evaluate the following statements on the third dimension of digitization:
statements: The third dimension concerns the result of value creation and asks how products and services can be extended through technology.
"Smart" here means the digitization of products and services — from a simple addition through to a lastingly changed customer experience.
In the simplest case, digitization can be an addition to or extension of the offering.
In the best case, it shapes the customer's experience lasting.
A product already counts as smart if the brand name is extended with the word "digital", even without a change in benefit or experience.
tactical_explanations:
The result of value creation is the third axis. It is about how technology can extend products and services — not about internal accounting alone.

The statement is true.

Smart here means digitization of the offering. What is meant is extending products and services through technology, not merely an advertising slogan.

The statement is true.

Addition is the simple entry point. A PDF manual or similar extension is digitization in the simplest case, before the experience goes deeper.

The statement is true.

A lasting experience is the more ambitious case. Digitization can shape the customer experience so that loyalty and perception change.

The statement is true.

Renaming without benefit falls short. Smart is measured by addition, extension or experience — not by the word "digital" in the brand name alone.

The statement is false.

title: Lego analog and digital
context: Evaluate the following statements on the example of digitizing a Lego product:
statements: Lego is, at the starting point, an analog experience: free building or building from instructions.
Instructions as a PDF are an example of a simple digital addition to the analog product.
A digital exploration mission in which different toys emerge depending on the course of play extends the experience beyond a mere PDF manual.
Positive digitized customer experiences arise mainly from price cuts; digital product extensions play hardly any role in that.
Such an extended experience can feel smart, increase loyalty and count as a positively digitized customer experience.
tactical_explanations:
Analog is the starting point. Free building and building from instructions describe the classic Lego experience without a digital layer.

The statement is true.

PDF is a simple addition. Providing the instructions digitally extends the analog product without rebuilding the play itself.

The statement is true.

An exploration mission goes further. Depending on the course of the mission, different toys emerge — the experience itself is co-shaped digitally, not only the instructions.

The statement is true.

Experience-extending digitization counts. A price cut alone is not the lever described; digitally extending the product can increase loyalty and experience.

The statement is false.

Smart and loyalty belong together. The extended experience can feel smart and increase loyalty to the product — a positively digitized customer experience.

The statement is true.

title: Digitization strategy and digital business
context: Evaluate the following statements on strategy and digitization of the company:
statements: Companies can act along the three dimensions and concentrate on one or more of them.
From that, a digitization strategy can be derived that helps align future decisions with a clear vision.
Overall, this action leads to digitization of the company — digital business.
A digitization strategy mainly serves retrospective documentation of completed IT projects and hardly steers future decisions.
Digital business mainly means purchasing individual software modules in the IT department, independent of dimensions and strategy.
tactical_explanations:
Freedom of choice along the dimensions. Concentrating on one or more axes is envisaged and forms the basis for strategic action.

The statement is true.

Strategy bundles the direction. From the choice of dimensions, a digitization strategy can be derived that aligns decisions with a vision.

The statement is true.

Digital business is the overall picture. Acting along the dimensions leads to digitization of the company as a whole.

The statement is true.

Strategy aims forward. It is meant to support future decisions and follow a vision — not only to archive completed projects.

The statement is false.

A single module is not enough. Digital business means digitization of the company along the dimensions and the strategy, not an isolated software purchase.

The statement is false.

title: Successful digital transformation
context: Evaluate the following statements on what successful digitization rests on:
statements: Successful digitization and digital transformation rest mainly on extending sensible aspects of the company through digital technologies.
These aspects include, among others, the sequence of work steps, communication and taking customer needs into account.
The transformation should not stand in the way of benefit.
Benefit and experience of a product or service should be extended as innovatively as possible.
Successful digitization is measured mainly by mirroring as many paper forms as PDFs as possible — regardless of whether processes or the customer experience improve.
tactical_explanations:
Extend sensible aspects. Successful transformation rests on digitally extending work steps, communication, customer needs and the like in a sensible way — not technology for technology's sake.

The statement is true.

The list is illustrative but accurate. Sequence, communication and customer needs are expressly among the aspects that should be digitally extended.

The statement is true.

Transformation should not block. It should support benefit and experience, not stand in the way as an end in itself.

The statement is true.

Extend benefit and experience. The goal is as innovative an extension as possible of the product or service from the customer's point of view.

The statement is true.

PDF mirroring alone is not enough. Success depends on sensible extension of processes and experience, not on a mere format change from paper to file.

The statement is false.

title: Assigning examples to the dimensions
context: Evaluate the following statements on assigning typical examples to the three dimensions:
statements: The digitally supported order flow behind the scenes at a bookseller such as Thalia belongs to the first dimension (backstage).
Humanic's 3D foot scanner mainly illustrates the frontstage because user wishes are taken into account more purposefully.
A PDF manual for a Lego set is an example of digitizing a product and thus of the third dimension.
Value creation arises mainly through social-media advertising and hardly through the economic use of resources behind the scenes.
A process model in purchasing replaces the frontstage because visual representations automatically capture customer needs.
tactical_explanations:
Backstage example. Internal order handling with system support is the first dimension — processes behind the scenes.

The statement is true.

Frontstage example. The foot scanner captures fit wishes and aims at the customer interface, not at internal warehouse control alone.

The statement is true.

Product digitization. The PDF manual extends the analog product and falls under the third dimension.

The statement is true.

Value creation begins behind the scenes with the economic use of resources. Social-media advertising does not replace this internal creation.

The statement is false.

Process model and frontstage are different. A visual representation of internal flows communicates processes; it neither replaces the customer interface nor automatically captures customer needs.

The statement is false.

title: Customer types and process end
context: Evaluate the following statements on customer concepts and the end of digitally supported workflows:
statements: A public institution can, in the frontstage sense, be a customer of a company.
Another company can also be a customer.
As soon as the customer is informed about the order status, the business process counts as finished — delivery or pickup are then no longer the defined end.
In the Thalia example, the process ends with delivery or readiness for pickup.
Depending on stock levels, further processes can be triggered internally and status information given to the customer.
tactical_explanations:
A public institution counts. The frontstage customer concept covers private person, company and public institution.

The statement is true.

B2B is envisaged. Another company can be a customer; frontstage is not limited to end consumers.

The statement is true.

A status message does not end the process. Information accompanies the flow; the defined end remains delivery or readiness for pickup.

The statement is false.

Two possible ends, both defined. Delivery or readiness for pickup close the order process described.

The statement is true.

Stock levels can trigger further workflows. A status message accompanies the process but does not replace the defined end.

The statement is true.

title: Digitization, dimensions and benefit
context: Evaluate the following statements on the link between digitization, dimensions and customer experience:
statements: Digitization as the application of digital technology drives digital transformation as change.
The three dimensions — backstage processes, frontstage toward the customer, digitization of products and services — structure starting points in the company.
Digital business means digitization of the company as a whole that follows from acting along these dimensions.
A process model replaces value creation: anyone who visually maps purchasing thereby already produces the product for the customer.
A simple digital addition such as a PDF manual is the same as an experience-extending digital mission; the difference between addition and deeper extension plays no role.
tactical_explanations:
Application and change belong together but remain distinguishable. Digitization drives transformation but does not replace the term.

The statement is true.

Three dimensions order the starting points. Backstage, frontstage and product/service digitization form the grid.

The statement is true.

Digital business is the overall picture from acting on the dimensions and strategy — not a single IT project.

The statement is true.

Mapping is not producing. A process model communicates workflows; value creation arises through the economic use of resources and the creation of services, not through the drawing alone.

The statement is false.

Addition and experience extension differ. A PDF manual is the simple case; a digital mission that co-shapes the course goes beyond that.

The statement is false.

title: Concept of digitization and digital transformation
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Digitization stands for the application of digital information and communication technology.
Digital transformation means the change thereby triggered in the economy, administration and the private sphere.
Both terms can be swapped without loss of meaning because application and change mean the same thing.
Digitization mainly concerns internal cost accounting and leaves customer relationships largely untouched.
As soon as hardware is present, the question of changed processes or offerings disappears.
tactical_explanations:
Application of digital ICT is the core of digitization — use in processes, not mere ownership.

The statement is true.

Transformation is the change that this application triggers. Economy, administration and the private sphere are the fields named.

The statement is true.

Tool and effect remain distinguishable. Digitization and digital transformation are linked but are not synonyms without a difference in meaning.

The statement is false.

Customer contact, processes and offerings belong to it. Narrowing it to cost accounting cuts out central fields of impact.

The statement is false.

Hardware alone is not enough. Transformation is measured by change in processes and offerings, not by the device inventory.

The statement is false.

title: Ubiquity of digital systems
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: In everyday life and in companies one encounters digital systems in many areas — from smart home technology to warehouse and production systems.
The English term ubiquitous computing describes the ubiquity of computing systems.
Business informatics deals with how technology supports and what effects that has on society, the economy and personal life.
Digital systems play hardly any role in a company context; they mainly concern the private household.
As soon as one gets up in the morning, contact with digital systems ends for the rest of the working day.
tactical_explanations:
Ubiquity in everyday life and at work. From the alarm clock via streaming to warehouse and production systems, the broad use of digital technology shows.

The statement is true.

Ubiquitous computing means ubiquity. The term summarises that computing systems can hardly be imagined away anymore.

The statement is true.

Business informatics looks at support and impact. Technology, society, the economy and personal life belong in the same view.

The statement is true.

Companies are full of digital systems. Warehouse recording, delivery positioning or production control show business use; limiting it to the household falls short.

The statement is false.

Contact continues. In working and company life too, digital systems remain present; the morning is only the entry.

The statement is false.

title: Technology changes entrepreneurial action
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Technology changes how companies act commercially — for example in processes, customer contact and offerings.
Internal process control is among the fields that can shift through technology.
The design of products and services and their market introduction can also be affected.
For such changes, the terms digitization or digital transformation are often used.
Technology leaves the way companies do business essentially unchanged and only affects office decoration.
tactical_explanations:
Broad influence on entrepreneurial action. Processes, customer relationships and the market offering belong to the fields of impact named.

The statement is true.

Internal control counts. Efficient process management behind the scenes is a central application field of digital technology.

The statement is true.

The offering side is included. Design and market introduction of products and services can change through technology.

The statement is true.

The terms are used precisely for these shifts and name application and change.

The statement is true.

Doing business itself changes. Technology intervenes in processes, customer contact and offerings — not only in the look of the office.

The statement is false.

title: Business process — basic definition
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: A business process consists of several logically connected activities and contributes toward a business objective.
Business processes can be carried out repeatedly.
Business processes have a clearly defined start and one or more defined ends.
Within a process, people can keep an overview and make decisions more purposefully.
A business process is a one-off project event without repeatability and without reference to a business objective.
tactical_explanations:
Several activities and a contribution to a goal belong together. Without logical connection and value toward a goal, the structure of a business process is missing.

The statement is true.

Repeatability is envisaged. Typical workflows such as order handling are meant as patterns that can start again.

The statement is true.

Start and one or more ends belong to it. Several clear endings of the same workflow are allowed.

The statement is true.

Overview and decision-making are benefits of a process view. Digital support helps decide relevantly and faster.

The statement is true.

A one-off event without a goal reference does not match the definition. Business processes are repeatable, goal-related workflows.

The statement is false.

title: Three dimensions of digitization at a glance
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Three dimensions illustrate digital opportunities for change in the company: backstage, frontstage and products/services.
Backstage means business processes behind the scenes that support value creation.
Frontstage means the connection between customers and the company.
The third dimension concerns digitization of the result of value creation — products and services.
The three dimensions describe only the internal IT department and leave customers and products aside.
tactical_explanations:
Three axes form the grid. Processes, customer interface and digitized offering structure the starting points.

The statement is true.

Backstage supports value creation. Internal processes are increasingly extended and controlled by systems.

The statement is true.

Frontstage is the outward side toward the customer — external focus and designing offerings with users in mind.

The statement is true.

Third dimension = result. Technology extends products and services, from a simple add-on to a changed experience.

The statement is true.

Customers and products belong to it. Frontstage and the third dimension are expressly part of the grid; limiting it to the IT department falls short.

The statement is false.

title: Backstage: internal value creation and processes
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The internal focus lies on the economic use of resources to create products and services.
Value creation here means that value is created through the economic use of resources.
Business processes behind the scenes support value creation and are increasingly extended and controlled by systems.
Digitally supported work steps lead to a digitally supported business process.
Backstage means the public customer interface; internal workflows fall under the third dimension.
tactical_explanations:
Resources are converted internally into services. The internal focus is creation behind the scenes, not the shop window.

The statement is true.

Creating value means value creation. The process behind the scenes is named that way; marketing rhetoric without creation is not enough.

The statement is true.

Processes carry value creation and are extended by systems. Digital control extends behind-the-scenes workflows but does not erase them.

The statement is true.

Digitally supported business process is the fitting expression for digitally supported work steps in the flow.

The statement is true.

Backstage is behind the scenes, not the customer interface. Frontstage is the connection to the customer; the third dimension concerns products and services.

The statement is false.

title: Frontstage: customer orientation and customer types
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The frontstage is the connection between customers and the company and the external focus.
Requirements and needs of users are in the foreground; offerings are designed with the customer in mind.
Depending on the setting, a private person, a company or a public institution can count as a customer.
Digitization offers potential to take user wishes into account more efficiently and more purposefully.
Frontstage is limited to internal warehouse accounting; customer wishes play no role there.
tactical_explanations:
Outward side toward the customer. External focus and connection to the company describe the second dimension.

The statement is true.

User wishes steer design. Offerings with the customer in mind and orientation toward requirements belong to the frontstage.

The statement is true.

Three customer types are envisaged. Private person, company or public institution — the variety belongs to the concept.

The statement is true.

New potential is the point. Digitization is meant to take wishes on board more accurately and efficiently.

The statement is true.

Warehouse accounting is backstage. Frontstage aims at customer relationships and user wishes, not at internal inventory control alone.

The statement is false.

title: Documentation and process model
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Documenting a process through a digital system helps communicate the workflow in the company.
A process model as a visual representation can give a first overview of a central workflow.
Within a process, people can keep an overview and make decisions more purposefully.
Process models also serve new employees for orientation — for example when joining purchasing.
Documentation and process model are the same as the running business process itself: anyone who draws purchasing has already executed it.
tactical_explanations:
Recording makes it communicable. Digital documentation supports passing on process knowledge.

The statement is true.

A visual representation helps with entry. Especially new employees can grasp a central workflow faster this way.

The statement is true.

Overview and decision-making belong to the benefits of digitally supported processes.

The statement is true.

Internal orientation is the purpose — including interns and new employees.

The statement is true.

Model and process are distinguishable. The process model is the visual representation; the business process is the running, goal-related workflow. Mapping does not replace execution.

The statement is false.

title: Smart products and services
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The third dimension deals with the result of value creation and its extension through technology.
Smart here means the digitization of products and services.
In the simplest case this can be an addition or extension; in the best case it shapes the customer experience lasting.
Companies can derive a digitization strategy along one or more dimensions.
The third dimension mainly concerns employees' payroll and not products or services.
tactical_explanations:
The result of value creation is the third axis — digitally extending products and services.

The statement is true.

Smart = digitization of the offering, from addition through to shaping the experience.

The statement is true.

The span from simple to lasting is envisaged. PDF addition and experience-shaping extension are different intensities.

The statement is true.

Strategy from the choice of dimensions. One or more dimensions can carry the vision for future decisions.

The statement is true.

Payroll is not the third dimension. It is aimed at products and services as the result of value creation.

The statement is false.

title: Business informatics and digital systems in companies
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: In a supermarket, systems can automatically record how many products are still in stock and whether reorder is needed.
Delivery services can use positioning and notification systems to communicate location as promptly as possible.
In production, systems help control process flows and detect problems quickly.
Business informatics deals, among other things, with how technology supports and what effects that has.
Digital systems in companies mainly serve to entertain the workforce and have hardly any link to automation or optimisation.
tactical_explanations:
Warehouse recording is a business example. Automatic inventory control and reordering show digital systems behind the scenes.

The statement is true.

Delivery services use positioning and notification. Digital systems communicate location as promptly as possible.

The statement is true.

Production is controlled and monitored. Systems help steer workflows and detect disruptions early.

The statement is true.

Support and impact belong to the subject of business informatics — in society, the economy and personal life.

The statement is true.

Not only entertainment. Digital systems serve automation, optimisation and support of business workflows.

The statement is false.

title: Example of a digital business process (online order)
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: For an online order, steps are triggered in the background so that the product can be made available quickly.
An internal system summarises the order and notifies available employees for further steps.
Detail steps can include warehouse retrieval, product selection and preparation for pickup or shipping.
Depending on stock levels, further processes can be triggered internally and status information given to the customer.
The digitally supported order process has neither a clear start nor a defined end; start and end are arbitrary.
tactical_explanations:
Background steps start with the order. The shop click triggers internal work but is not yet fulfilment.

The statement is true.

System and assignment interlock. Summarising and notifying steer the flow behind the scenes.

The statement is true.

Concrete detail steps belong to the example. Warehouse, selection and shipping or pickup preparation are typical.

The statement is true.

Stock levels can trigger further workflows. A status message accompanies the process but does not replace the end.

The statement is true.

Business processes have a clearly defined start and one or more defined ends. Arbitrariness without start and end contradicts the definition.

The statement is false.

title: Taking customer wishes into account more purposefully
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Fit questions when buying shoes — size, width and the like — often cost time and nerves.
A 3D foot scanner can record users' requirements and store them in the customer account.
In store and online, the digital footprint can be matched against the desired model.
Such services show the potential of digitization to take user wishes into account more purposefully.
Frontstage potential of digitization exists only offline in the store and cannot in principle be used online.
tactical_explanations:
Fit remains the challenge. That is exactly where the service starts.

The statement is true.

Scanner and account store the digital footprint for later use.

The statement is true.

Matching in store and online enables better fit decisions.

The statement is true.

Frontstage potential: take wishes on board more efficiently and purposefully — online as well as in store.

The statement is true.

The service described uses the same digital footprint precisely in store and via app or online. Limiting it to offline alone falls short.

The statement is false.

title: Digitization strategy and digital business
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Companies can concentrate on one or more of the three dimensions.
From that, a digitization strategy can be derived that aligns future decisions with a vision.
Overall this leads to digital business — digitization of the company.
Successful transformation extends sensible aspects such as work steps, communication and customer needs through digital technologies.
Digital business mainly means buying a single software module without reference to dimensions or strategy.
tactical_explanations:
Freedom of choice: one or more dimensions are allowed.

The statement is true.

Strategy bundles the direction for future decisions.

The statement is true.

Digital business is the overall picture of company digitization.

The statement is true.

Sensible extension rather than technology for technology's sake — the success criterion.

The statement is true.

A single module without reference to dimensions and strategy is not enough for digital business.

The statement is false.

title: Fine distinctions: process ends and value contribution
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: A business process has only exactly one defined end; several defined ends are ruled out.
Business processes can be carried out repeatedly and contribute toward a business objective.
A clearly defined start belongs to a business process.
In the order example, delivery and readiness for pickup can be two defined ends of the same workflow.
As soon as the customer receives a status message, the business process is finished regardless of delivery or pickup.
tactical_explanations:
Several ends are allowed. The definition names one or more defined ends — not only exactly one.

The statement is false.

Repeatability and contribution to a goal belong to the definition of a business process.

The statement is true.

A clear start is a required element alongside the defined ends.

The statement is true.

Two endings, one process. Pickup and shipping can be alternative defined ends.

The statement is true.

Status is accompaniment, not completion. The end remains delivery or readiness for pickup.

The statement is false.

title: Separating the dimensions cleanly
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Backstage and frontstage denote the same dimension: internal warehouse control and the customer interface fall together.
Backstage means business processes behind the scenes that support value creation.
Frontstage means the connection between customers and the company.
The third dimension concerns the digitization of products and services.
A process model in purchasing replaces the frontstage because visual representations automatically capture customer needs.
tactical_explanations:
The dimensions are separate. Backstage = behind the scenes, frontstage = customer interface. Merging them mixes internal control and customer relationships.

The statement is false.

Backstage supports value creation through internal processes and systems.

The statement is true.

Frontstage is the outward side toward the customer.

The statement is true.

Third dimension = digitally extended offering.

The statement is true.

A process model communicates workflows behind the scenes; it neither replaces the customer interface nor automatically captures user wishes.

The statement is false.

title: Reach of digitization and concept trap
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Digitization and digital transformation reach into the economy, administration and the private sphere.
Technology can change processes, customer relationships and product design at the same time.
Companies can develop a digitization strategy along one or more dimensions.
Digital transformation counts as complete as soon as a computer stands somewhere in the business — regardless of processes and offerings.
The three dimensions concern only the IT department and leave customers and products aside.
tactical_explanations:
Broad reach. Economy, administration and the private sphere are the fields of change named.

The statement is true.

Several fields of impact at once. Internal control, frontstage and offering can be affected in parallel.

The statement is true.

Strategy from the choice of dimensions is envisaged.

The statement is true.

A computer inventory alone is not enough. Transformation is measured by change in processes and offerings.

The statement is false.

Customers and products belong to the grid. Frontstage and the third dimension are expressly part of the three dimensions.

The statement is false.

title: Smart vs. mere addition
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: A PDF manual for an analog product is an example of a simple digital addition.
A digital exploration mission that co-shapes the course of play goes beyond a mere PDF addition.
In the best case, digitization shapes the customer experience lasting and can increase loyalty.
Smart is limited to extending the brand name with "digital" without changing benefit or experience.
Positive digitized customer experiences arise only from price cuts, not from digital product extension.
tactical_explanations:
Simple addition: a digital document for the analog core product.

The statement is true.

Experience extension goes deeper than a format change of the instructions.

The statement is true.

Lasting shaping and loyalty are the more ambitious case of "smart".

The statement is true.

Renaming without benefit falls short. Smart is measured by addition, extension or experience.

The statement is false.

Digitally extending the product counts. A price cut alone is not the lever described for positively digitized experiences.

The statement is false.

title: Exam pressure: dimensions, strategy and success criterion
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Companies may concentrate on exactly one dimension only; several at once are ruled out.
From work along the dimensions, a digitization strategy can be derived.
Successful transformation extends sensible aspects in the company through digital technologies.
Successful digitization is measured mainly by replacing as many paper forms as possible with PDFs — regardless of benefit and experience.
Benefit and experience of a product or service should be extended as innovatively as possible.
tactical_explanations:
One or more dimensions are allowed. The claim "exactly one only" is too narrow.

The statement is false.

Strategy follows from the choice of dimensions and vision.

The statement is true.

Sensible extension — work steps, communication, customer needs — is the success criterion.

The statement is true.

PDF mirroring alone is not enough. Success depends on benefit and experience, not on a mere format change.

The statement is false.

Extending innovatively is the goal: transformation should not stand in the way of benefit.

The statement is true.

title: Customer concept, ends and internal control under exam pressure
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: As a frontstage customer, only a private person comes into question; companies and public institutions do not count.
A business process has only exactly one defined end; alternative endings of the same workflow are not allowed.
Internal process control is among the fields that technology can change.
Public institutions and other companies can be customers.
In the order example, the process ends with delivery or readiness for pickup.
tactical_explanations:
Three customer types are envisaged. Private person, company and public institution belong to the frontstage customer concept.

The statement is false.

One or more defined ends are allowed — not only exactly one.

The statement is false.

Backstage control is a central field of impact of digital technology.

The statement is true.

B2B and public demand are expressly included.

The statement is true.

Two possible ends close the order process described.

The statement is true.

title: Overall link of digital transformation
context: Analyse digital transformation and digitization in companies. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Digitization means application of digital technology; digital transformation means the change thereby triggered.
Three dimensions — backstage, frontstage, products/services — structure starting points in the company.
Digitization and digital transformation are interchangeable synonyms without a difference in meaning.
Companies can derive a strategy along the dimensions and thereby aim for digital business.
Successful transformation rests on extending sensible aspects through digital technologies and strengthening benefit as well as experience.
tactical_explanations:
Application and change remain distinguishable but are linked.

The statement is true.

Three dimensions order the starting points clearly.

The statement is true.

Swapping as synonyms mixes tool and effect. The terms are coupled but not identical in meaning.

The statement is false.

Strategy and digital business follow from acting on the dimensions and from vision.

The statement is true.

Sensible extension plus benefit and experience — the success criterion of transformation.

The statement is true.

title: Digitized products and services
context: Evaluate the following statements on how digitization changes products and services:
statements: Many products and services have changed through digitization — for example digital tickets or grocery deliveries to the home.
The use of IT changes products, services and business models and can make new models possible in the first place.
Digital additions such as apps or delivery services typically leave the underlying business model unchanged.
Examples such as the Wiener Linien app or grocery delivery services show new possibilities based on technology.
Digital channels only affect the look of the website; production, provision and distribution remain untouched by them.
tactical_explanations:
Everyday examples show the change. Managing tickets digitally or having groceries delivered relies on technology and changes use and offering.

The statement is true.

IT intervenes in offering and model. Products, services and business models shift; some models only arise through IT.

The statement is true.

New possibilities often change the business model as well — not only the surface. Digital channels and delivery logic can reorder production, provision and distribution.

The statement is false.

Concrete examples support the point. App tickets and grocery delivery illustrate technology-supported offerings.

The statement is true.

IT affects creation, provision and distribution — not only website look. Anyone who sees only the surface misses the model change.

The statement is false.

title: What a business model describes
context: Evaluate the following statements on the definition of the business model:
statements: A business model describes how a company, on the basis of a business idea, produces, provides and distributes a product or service.
The goal, after comparing resources used and revenues, is a profit — that is, value creation.
A business model is limited to the advertising graphics of the website and says nothing about production, provision or distribution.
The use of IT can create new possibilities to produce, provide and distribute products and services via business processes.
Value creation in the business model means only selling advertising space; producing and distributing the offering play no role.
tactical_explanations:
Production, provision and distribution form the core of what a business model describes.

The statement is true.

Resources and revenues are compared; profit or value creation is the target picture.

The statement is true.

Advertising graphics alone are not a business model. It is about the economic logic from creation through to distribution and about comparing input and revenues.

The statement is false.

IT opens new paths in the same steps: create, provide, distribute — supported by processes.

The statement is true.

Value creation arises from production, provision and distribution in the balancing of resources and revenues — not only from advertising space.

The statement is false.

title: IT use and value creation
context: Evaluate the following statements on the causal link between IT use and value creation:
statements: IT use creates new possibilities to produce, provide and distribute products and services with the help of business processes.
Building on that, value can be generated for companies and customers.
This value can be multiplied through technology — for example when more customers are reached or offerings are individualised.
IT use and value creation stand in no causal link; technology remains irrelevant for production and distribution.
Business processes play no role in creating and distributing digitally supported offerings.
tactical_explanations:
IT opens possibilities along the process chain from creation through to distribution.

The statement is true.

Value for both sides can build on that — companies and customers.

The statement is true.

Reach and individualisation are typical levers of multiplication.

The statement is true.

The causal link is central: IT use and value creation interlock; technology is not irrelevant.

The statement is false.

Business processes remain the framework through which creation, provision and distribution run — including when digitally supported.

The statement is false.

title: Classic webshop
context: Evaluate the following statements on the webshop as a technology-based business model:
statements: A classic webshop makes it possible to order products directly online — for example at Amazon.de or Zalando.de.
In the webshop, goods are sold directly to customers or to individual companies.
The webshop is typically operated by one seller.
A webshop is the same as an online marketplace because typically many independent private sellers operate the platform there.
Online ordering and digital distribution play no role for technology-based business models.
tactical_explanations:
Webshop = direct online distribution by the operator. The retailers named are typical examples.

The statement is true.

Sales go to end customers or companies — B2C and B2B are possible.

The statement is true.

One seller operates the shop; that distinguishes it from a marketplace with many providers.

The statement is true.

Webshop and marketplace differ. On a marketplace, private persons also have access to offer; the shop is operated by one seller.

The statement is false.

Online ordering is precisely a core example of technology-based models.

The statement is false.

title: Online marketplace
context: Evaluate the following statements on the online marketplace as distinct from the webshop:
statements: An online marketplace is an online environment for buyers and sellers through which products can be traded.
In contrast to the webshop, private persons here also have access to offer and sell products.
willhaben.at and eBay.de are examples of such marketplaces.
The marketplace operator provides access for customer and seller via a platform; interested parties can search and negotiate prices.
A marketplace operator provides neither platform nor access; buyers and sellers must find each other without digital mediation.
tactical_explanations:
Marketplace = digital environment for both sides of the market.

The statement is true.

Private persons can offer — that distinguishes it from the classic one-seller webshop.

The statement is true.

willhaben and eBay are typical examples.

The statement is true.

The operator provides access; search and contact between the sides belong to the model.

The statement is true.

Platform and access are precisely the operator's service. Without digital mediation, the model described is missing.

The statement is false.

title: Virtual environment and social network
context: Evaluate the following statements on social networks as a digital business model:
statements: A digital business model can consist in offering a virtual environment — an online community or social network.
Facebook, X and LinkedIn are examples of this.
People with the same areas of interest can exchange and get in touch with friends.
Such models earn, among other things, by selling advertising space.
An online community requires that all members stand at the same time in the same physical store and exchange goods there.
tactical_explanations:
Virtual environment / social network is a named model.

The statement is true.

The platforms named are examples of online communities.

The statement is true.

Exchange and staying in touch are the core of use.

The statement is true.

Advertising space is a typical revenue source of this model type.

The statement is true.

A physical store is not a requirement. The community is online; the model lives from digital networking, not from a shared store location.

The statement is false.

title: Pure-play business models
context: Evaluate the following statements on pure-play business models:
statements: Many of the models mentioned count as pure-play because they take place mainly online.
Such companies operate primarily in the digital space and have no physical store locations in the sense of a shop for physical inspection.
Many of these business models only became possible through the Internet.
Pure-play refers to the purity grade of raw materials and not to the venue of the business model.
Clicks-and-mortar and pure-play are identical because both forgo store branches.
tactical_explanations:
Pure-play = predominantly digital venue. Online models without a physical branch fall under it.

The statement is true.

No shop for physical inspection — that is what distinguishes pure-play from mixed models.

The statement is true.

The Internet as enabler of many of these models is part of the description.

The statement is true.

Pure-play means the digital venue of the business, not raw-material purity.

The statement is false.

Clicks-and-mortar digitally complements the physical business; pure-play forgoes such branches. The models are not identical.

The statement is false.

title: Clicks and mortar
context: Evaluate the following statements on clicks-and-mortar business models:
statements: With clicks-and-mortar, the digital presence — for example a website or platform — complements the traditional physical business.
Thalia with store branches and an online shop is an example of clicks-and-mortar.
A clicks-and-mortar company must not show customers any goods in the store; physical inspection is ruled out.
Pure-play and clicks-and-mortar are alternative names for the same purely online model.
A website or platform can be the digital side of this extension.
tactical_explanations:
Digital complements physical — that is clicks-and-mortar.

The statement is true.

Thalia with store and online shop illustrates exactly this combination.

The statement is true.

Physical inspection is precisely part of the traditional business that is complemented digitally — not ruled out.

The statement is false.

Pure-play is mainly online without a branch; clicks-and-mortar combines both. Not synonyms.

The statement is false.

Website or platform are typical digital complements.

The statement is true.

title: Music industry and iTunes
context: Evaluate the following statements on how Apple and iTunes changed the music industry:
statements: Today's music industry differs substantially from that around the year 2000; providers have changed models based on ICT several times.
In the past one typically bought whole albums on physical media; later, legal online distribution also enabled purchasing individual tracks.
With the iPod and the iTunes Store, Apple strongly shaped the legal distribution of individual tracks.
Spotify and the iTunes Store followed the same subscription streaming model from the start, with neither downloads nor per-track sales.
Thick plastic CD cases replace information and communication technology as the cause of legal online distribution of individual tracks.
tactical_explanations:
Industry change through ICT. Models were rebuilt several times — from physical media to download and streaming.

The statement is true.

Album on a carrier vs. individual tracks online — that is the transition described.

The statement is true.

iTunes and the iPod stand for legal per-track sales and new playback devices.

The statement is true.

Different steps: iTunes stood for download/per-track sales; Spotify later for streaming subscriptions. Equating them blurs the change.

The statement is false.

ICT — not the CD case — carries legal online distribution. The case belongs to the old physical-media model.

The statement is false.

title: Spotify and streaming subscriptions
context: Evaluate the following statements on Spotify's business model compared with per-track sales:
statements: Spotify changed music consumption by offering tracks as streams rather than for download.
The model is built on a subscription, no longer on purchasing individual tracks.
Through the subscription, users get access to a very large catalog of available audio titles.
Streaming on Spotify requires that every track be burned to a CD and mailed before listening.
Spotify's subscription model is financed mainly by selling concert stages to cities.
tactical_explanations:
Streaming instead of download is the next step after per-track sales.

The statement is true.

Subscription replaces individual purchase as the central logic.

The statement is true.

Broad catalog access through membership is the benefit of the subscription.

The statement is true.

Streaming runs digitally via the platform — not via CD burning and postal shipping per title.

The statement is false.

Subscription fees (and possibly ads in freemium variants) carry the model; selling concert stages to cities is not the logic described.

The statement is false.

title: Revenue model as part of the business model
context: Evaluate the following statements on the revenue model:
statements: The revenue model concerns how the company makes money — generates income and earns profit.
Technology influences how the revenue model can be designed.
Companies can focus on one revenue model or combine several.
In the context of digitization, the advertising model and the subscription model are two especially important revenue models.
The revenue model replaces the production and provision of products and is not an aspect of the business model.
tactical_explanations:
Making money is the core of the revenue model — income and profit.

The statement is true.

Technology opens new design options for income logics.

The statement is true.

Focus or combination are both provided for.

The statement is true.

Advertising and subscription are the two highlighted models in the digital context.

The statement is true.

The revenue model is an aspect of the business model, but it does not replace production and provision.

The statement is false.

title: Advertising model and seemingly free services
context: Evaluate the following statements on the advertising model:
statements: The advertising model relies on advertising as a revenue source: high visitor numbers enable income from ads.
Website covers forms such as news, web shops, social networks, or other platforms.
Many services that feel "free" — for example search, classifieds, or price comparison — rely on the advertising model.
The advertising model is considered barely used and has hardly shaped the online experience.
Today's online experience would likely have remained identical if an entirely different revenue model had prevailed instead of the advertising model.
tactical_explanations:
Advertising in exchange for reach. Many visitors make ad slots valuable.

The statement is true.

Website is broadly framed: news, shops, networks, and further platforms.

The statement is true.

The "free" feel is often ad-funded. Search, classified portals, and comparison portals are typical cases.

The statement is true.

The advertising model is one of the most popular and strongly shapes the online experience — not barely used.

The statement is false.

A different revenue model would have shaped the experience differently. The account emphasizes precisely advertising's formative role.

The statement is false.

title: Digital advertising slots
context: Evaluate the following statements on forms of digital advertising:
statements: Search engines can sell advertising slots among other things via keywords in search or ads tied to search terms.
Comparison portals can offer banner advertising and combine it with search terms.
Online daily newspapers use the advertising model among other things to cover operating costs of content.
Various digital advertising formats can appear on the home pages of online daily newspapers.
Digital advertising slots require that search engines and portals remain invisible to advertisers and show no ads.
tactical_explanations:
Keyword and ad sales are typical forms for search engines.

The statement is true.

Banner plus search-term combination is a named pattern for comparison portals.

The statement is true.

Advertising helps finance newspapers' online content.

The statement is true.

Various ad formats on the home page are common and are cited as an example.

The statement is true.

Ad slots are precisely visible to advertisers and users; invisibility contradicts the model.

The statement is false.

title: Alphabet and the share of advertising
context: Evaluate the following statements on Alphabet's quarterly revenues and the online advertising market:
statements: Alphabet is the parent company of Google and further Google companies.
In a named quarter of 2023, revenue was around 86 billion dollars, a large share of it from advertising — illustrating the strength of the advertising model.
From the same orders of magnitude, the advertising share is on the order of about three quarters of quarterly revenue.
Of 86.3 billion dollars in quarterly revenue, only about 8.6 billion dollars came from advertising — roughly 10 percent.
The online advertising market is a strongly represented model; large groups such as Alphabet serve as an illustrative example.
tactical_explanations:
Alphabet as parent company is the framing behind Google and related businesses.

The statement is true.

The order of magnitude — high revenue, of which a large advertising block — is meant to show the importance of the advertising model, not to replace the accounts.

The statement is true.

65.5 of 86.3 billion corresponds to about 75 percent — three quarters as an order of magnitude.

The statement is true.

10 percent would be far below the stated advertising share. The illustration cites about 65.5 of 86.3 billion, i.e. roughly three quarters — not one tenth.

The statement is false.

A strongly represented advertising model — Alphabet as an example of market importance.

The statement is true.

title: Subscription model and combination with advertising
context: Evaluate the following statements on the subscription model and combined revenues:
statements: The subscription model charges an ongoing fee for access to part or all of the offerings.
Netflix and Spotify are classic examples; with a subscription, customers get access to the platform's content.
Many companies that previously used other revenue models have adapted the subscription model.
Content providers such as newspapers today rely entirely only on completely ad-free free offerings with no fee at all.
Software providers such as Adobe can shift revenue models toward ongoing fees and away from classic one-time purchase.
tactical_explanations:
Ongoing fee for access — that is the subscription model.

The statement is true.

Streaming examples illustrate full access through membership.

The statement is true.

Adaptation of earlier models is expressly described.

The statement is true.

Newspapers often rely on subscription or on a combination of advertising and subscription — not entirely on ad-free free offerings.

The statement is false.

Adobe example: shift from one-time purchase to ongoing fees.

The statement is true.

title: Adobe, subscription shift, and industry transformation
context: Evaluate the following statements on Adobe's model shift and digital transformation of industries:
statements: In 2013 Adobe switched from the classic revenue model (one-time purchase) to a subscription model.
Previously one could acquire individual packages such as Photoshop for life through a single payment.
Nowadays a monthly or annual fee is typically required for use.
Adobe offers little software for image editing, photography, film, or graphics; the subscription shift mainly concerned office furniture.
Through digitization, entire industries are transformed — with products, services, and business models — not merely file formats exchanged.
tactical_explanations:
2013 marks Adobe's switch to the subscription model.

The statement is true.

One-time purchase with lifelong use was the earlier pattern.

The statement is true.

An ongoing fee is today's usage pattern for many Creative Cloud products.

The statement is true.

Adobe is precisely strong in creative software; the shift concerns software use, not office furniture.

The statement is false.

Industry transformation goes beyond format swaps: models, offerings, and use change.

The statement is true.

title: The Internet as IT infrastructure
context: Evaluate the following statements on the Internet as a building block of digitization:
statements: The Internet is a central building block for realizing digitization.
It constitutes the most important IT infrastructure for supporting the global networking of people and companies.
The Internet mainly connects devices within a single building and practically ends at the property boundary.
The Internet is to be understood as a network of networks that are interconnected worldwide.
Private communication and business information exchange hardly ever build technically on the Internet.
tactical_explanations:
Without the Internet, the central carrier of many digital functions in private and business contexts is missing.

The statement is true.

Global networking rests on this infrastructure — people and companies.

The statement is true.

Worldwide connection, not just a building. Undersea cables and global nets show the reach beyond property boundaries.

The statement is false.

Network of networks — that is the key formulation for the Internet.

The statement is true.

Many private and business functions build on Internet technology — information exchange and communication.

The statement is false.

title: What a network is
context: Evaluate the following statements on the definition of a computer network:
statements: A computer network is a spatially distributed system of data stations that exchange data via communication facilities and paths.
A data station is a computer — for example a PC, tablet, or smartphone.
Communication facilities can be a WLAN module in the device or a router in the household.
A computer network requires that all data stations stand in the same room; spatial distribution is ruled out.
A network connects data stations without data being meant to be exchanged.
tactical_explanations:
Spatial distribution plus connection for data exchange — that is the computer network.

The statement is true.

PC, tablet, smartphone are typical data stations.

The statement is true.

WLAN module and router are examples of communication facilities.

The statement is true.

Spatial distribution is part of the definition — stations need not stand in the same room.

The statement is false.

Data exchange is the purpose of the connection; without it the network lacks meaning.

The statement is false.

title: Communication paths on the Internet
context: Evaluate the following statements on cable, wireless, and access to the Internet:
statements: The communication path can be implemented wirelessly or by cable.
As soon as data stations somehow seem "connected," neither a communication facility nor a communication path is needed.
Undersea cables connect continents with one another.
Internet access is only possible when sender and receiver stand in the same room.
In every case, access is to a network — the Internet.
tactical_explanations:
Cable and wireless are both provided paths.

The statement is true.

Facility and path remain necessary. Connection without communication facility and path is not a complete network description.

The statement is false.

Undersea cables are the example of continental connection.

The statement is true.

Global and wireless paths show: the same room is not a prerequisite.

The statement is false.

Access runs via the Internet network — regardless of the concrete path form.

The statement is true.

title: Internet and World Wide Web
context: Evaluate the following statements on the difference between the Internet and the WWW:
statements: The World Wide Web is an application or service that builds on the Internet's infrastructure.
The WWW enables providing information, making it findable, and presenting it meaningfully.
Internet and World Wide Web technically denote the same layer with no difference between carrier network and service.
The Internet is a huge network over which data can be sent and received.
Neither emails nor search queries nor messenger messages can run as data over the Internet.
tactical_explanations:
WWW = service on the Internet, not the network itself.

The statement is true.

Providing, finding, and presenting are the named WWW functions.

The statement is true.

Carrier and service differ. Internet = network; WWW = application on it. Everyday language often conflates them; technically they remain distinguishable.

The statement is false.

Sending and receiving data over the network is the core of the Internet.

The statement is true.

Email, search, and messenger use the Internet for transmission — they are data over the network.

The statement is false.

title: Everyday language, email, and further services
context: Evaluate the following statements on how services use the Internet:
statements: In everyday life and work, Internet and Web are often used as synonyms.
Someone researching on the Web with a browser often phrases it as researching "on the Internet."
When researching, a web browser typically only accesses local files without network access and not the WWW.
Email is another service that uses the Internet for transmission.
Messages via WhatsApp are not among the data that can be sent over the Internet.
tactical_explanations:
Colloquial language often conflates the terms — that is expressly noted.
