The statement is true.

Browser research on the Web is often called "Internet," but means the WWW service.

The statement is true.

Research via the browser targets the WWW over the network — not only local files without access.

The statement is false.

Email uses the Internet as a transmission network, but is not the same as the WWW.

The statement is true.

Messenger messages run as data over the Internet — they belong to the named examples.

The statement is false.

title: Tim Berners-Lee and CERN
context: Evaluate the following statements on the origins of the World Wide Web:
statements: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN.
In 1990 he published a scientific paper on it titled "Information Management: A Proposal."
The motivation originally lay in managing and exchanging research results at CERN with colleagues.
The original motivation was mainly selling online advertising to retail companies.
HTTP, HTML, and URL played no role for the WWW idea and only arose decades after 1989.
tactical_explanations:
1989 at CERN — that is the historical placement of the WWW invention.

The statement is true.

The 1990 paper carries exactly this title and presents the idea.

The statement is true.

Research exchange at CERN was the starting point — not advertising.

The statement is true.

Advertising to retailers was not the original motivation; it was about information management in research.

The statement is false.

HTTP, HTML, and URL are the fundamental concepts Berners-Lee communicated — central to a working WWW.

The statement is false.

title: HTTP, HTML, and URL
context: Evaluate the following statements on the fundamental concepts of the WWW:
statements: HTTP specifies which steps are needed for a browser to request information from a server.
HTML structures information so that a browser can display it and a human can read it.
The URL is a uniform system for addressing information — making it findable and retrievable.
HTTP mainly describes the color design of advertising banners and hardly the steps of a server request.
URLs mainly decorate web pages and hardly make resources findable.
tactical_explanations:
HTTP = communication rules for browser requests to servers.

The statement is true.

HTML = structure and presentation language for readable content.

The statement is true.

URL = uniform addressing of resources.

The statement is true.

HTTP governs request steps, not banner colors.

The statement is false.

URLs address and make findable — decoration is not their purpose.

The statement is false.

title: Communication protocol
context: Evaluate the following statements on the protocol in information technology:
statements: An IT protocol is not the same as meeting minutes.
Communication protocols apply only to human phone calls and not to data exchange between computers.
Among other things, the protocol records how messages must be formulated and replies designed.
Similar to the post, clear details of addressee and sender are needed in case the shipment cannot be delivered.
Which characters, contents, and representation sizes may be used remains entirely unregulated in an IT protocol.
tactical_explanations:
Two different protocol concepts. IT means communication rules between computers.

The statement is true.

IT protocols precisely govern data exchange between computers — not only human phone calls.

The statement is false.

Message and reply form belong to the recorded rules.

The statement is true.

Postal analogy: address and sender as clear conventions.

The statement is true.

Characters, contents, and representation sizes are regulated in the protocol — they do not remain unregulated.

The statement is false.

title: Browser, HTML, and hyperlinks
context: Evaluate the following statements on surfing the Web:
statements: When surfing the Web, the browser typically communicates with a server via HTTP.
Information is displayed in the browser among other things with the help of HTML.
Hyperlinks are placed URLs that point to further pages and make the Web a network of linked resources.
When surfing, the browser mainly communicates with the server by letter post and hardly via HTTP.
URLs do not address resources uniformly; each browser invents its own private addresses when surfing, without a locator system.
tactical_explanations:
Browser–server via HTTP is the typical surfing path.

The statement is true.

HTML carries the display in the browser.

The statement is true.

Hyperlinks link resources and make the Web a network.

The statement is true.

HTTP — not letter post — is the communication protocol when surfing.

The statement is false.

URL is precisely the uniform addressing system; private addresses without a locator contradict the concept.

The statement is false.

title: Request, response, and server
context: Evaluate the following statements on communication between browser and server:
statements: Using HTTP rules, the browser can request a file on a server.
A server is a computer that waits over the network for requests.
Server software processes requests and delivers a response to a request.
The reply turns out the same regardless of whether the HTML page is findable on the server or not.
The request-response principle is not part of the WWW's architecture.
tactical_explanations:
Request via HTTP rules is the start of the communication.

The statement is true.

A server waits on the network for requests — typically operated in a server room.

The statement is true.

Request and response form the pair of the server software's reply.

The statement is true.

The reply depends on whether the page is findable or not — it does not always turn out the same.

The statement is false.

Request-response is part of WWW architecture and client-server logic.

The statement is false.

title: Client-server architecture
context: Evaluate the following statements on the client and server model:
statements: Client-server architecture distinguishes between client and server.
Several applications can run on a server that provide services over a network.
Services over the Internet are mainly provided by the client; the server hardly delivers services.
A web browser is an example of a client.
Many interactions on the Internet no longer build on client-server architecture and request-response.
tactical_explanations:
Client and server are the two roles of the model.

The statement is true.

The server provides services; several applications can run on it.

The statement is true.

Services are provided by the server; the client requests — the roles are reversed if one makes the client the sole provider.

The statement is false.

Browser as client is the standard example.

The statement is true.

Many interactions continue to build on client-server and request-response.

The statement is false.

title: Services on the WWW
context: Evaluate the following statements about types of services on the web:
statements: Based on client–server and communication principles, various services can be provided on the WWW.
A comparison platform provides an overview of providers in a market.
A webshop handles orders; a content provider makes news available online.
Comparison platforms, webshops, and news offerings are barely technically feasible on the WWW and rarely occur there.
The options for offering services over the web are scarce and steadily shrinking.
tactical_explanations:
WWW services build on architecture and communication principles.

The statement is true.

Comparison platform = market overview for customers.

The statement is true.

Webshop and news offering are stated types of services.

The statement is true.

Exactly these services are typical WWW offerings — not technically impossible.

The statement is false.

Options are numerous and growing — not scarce and shrinking.

The statement is false.

title: Browsers and enterprise software
context: Evaluate the following statements about the interface for services on the internet:
statements: The web browser is the central interface for accessing services on the WWW.
Besides the web browser, other systems — for example enterprise software with network interfaces — can also provide access to internet services.
Machine-to-machine data exchange between businesses over the internet is ruled out, because only humans are allowed to type in a browser.
Enterprise software can have interfaces to communicate with other companies on the internet and exchange information.
Access to internet services is limited to public library computers and denied to private and business systems.
tactical_explanations:
The browser is the central WWW interface — but not the only possible one.

The statement is true.

The browser is central for WWW services, but not the only access path: enterprise software and machine-to-machine data exchange also use internet interfaces.

The statement is true.

Machine-to-machine exchange between businesses is expressly possible — not limited to humans typing in a browser.

The statement is false.

Enterprise software with internet interfaces is envisaged.

The statement is true.

Access is widespread — private and business — not limited to library computers.

The statement is false.

title: Internet economy
context: Evaluate the following statements about the economic use of the internet:
statements: Digital networks can create markets or extend them with digital places through which economic transactions run.
The internet economy covers the economic use of the internet for value-creating transactions.
A digital market or digital platform emerges in a digital network with different market participants.
Internet economy mainly means private entertainment without value-creating transactions — for example pure leisure chat with no market connection.
In this context, the internet does not become a new platform for companies.
tactical_explanations:
A digital place for economic transactions — create or extend a market.

The statement is true.

Value-creating transactions over the internet are the core of the internet economy.

The statement is true.

A digital market/platform with various participants is the result.

The statement is true.

The internet economy is more than private chat: it means economic use and value-creating transactions — not only entertainment without a market connection.

The statement is false.

The internet is precisely becoming a platform for companies where providers and customers interact.

The statement is false.

title: Platform operators and end customers
context: Evaluate the following statements about the internet as a platform and operators of digital markets:
statements: On the internet platform, providers and customers can interact with each other.
Sometimes additional platform operators are needed that offer a digital platform for a specific market.
For end customers it is usually immediately obvious that they are contacting other merchants via a platform operator.
For more than 30 years the internet has created a digital space in which numerous innovations can take place.
Platform operators are superfluous for digital markets, because providers and customers meet without mediation anyway in the same physical store.
tactical_explanations:
Exchange between the provider and customer sides is the purpose of the platform.

The statement is true.

Additional operators for specific markets are envisaged.

The statement is true.

Often the mediation is precisely not obvious to end customers — as the platform example shows. “Usually immediately obvious” overstates the case.

The statement is false.

Longer than three decades of digital space with innovations — that is the time frame.

The statement is true.

Digital mediation can be necessary; treating a physical store as the only meeting logic misses digital marketplaces.

The statement is false.

title: Refurbed and willhaben
context: Evaluate the following statements about the examples of digital marketplaces:
statements: Refurbed offers a digital marketplace for companies that sell used and professionally refurbished technology.
In the background, offers from available merchants are collected; customers can conclude a purchase contract with the respective merchant.
willhaben is another example: listings across various industries and contact between interested parties for transactions.
willhaben limits listings to exactly one industry and excludes other sectors of the economy.
After posting listings on willhaben, interested parties are not allowed to contact each other to complete transactions.
tactical_explanations:
Refurbed = digital marketplace for refurbished technology.

The statement is true.

Merchant offers in the background, contract with the merchant — the platform mediates.

The statement is true.

willhaben = listings across industries and contact for transactions.

The statement is true.

Various industries are envisaged — no restriction to exactly one.

The statement is false.

Contact between interested parties is part of the model so that transactions can take place.

The statement is false.

title: Topic areas of business informatics
context: Evaluate the following statements about which topics business informatics covers:
statements: Digitization in the corporate context, transformation of business models, and the effects of digital networks on transactions belong to the topics of business informatics.
The discipline is limited to exactly these three topics and has no further questions.
System design, management challenges, and ethical impacts in a digitized society also belong to it.
Understanding the role of business informatics is fundamental for shaping the associated systems in a sustainable way.
Business informatics mainly deals with optimizing tax forms and largely leaves digital networks and business models aside.
tactical_explanations:
The topics named are closely intertwined and fall within business informatics.

The statement is true.

The discipline covers more: system design, management, ethics, and further areas — not only three keywords.

The statement is false.

Design, management, and ethics are expressly named as further topics.

The statement is true.

A key role for future-proof system design — understanding is fundamental.

The statement is true.

Tax forms alone miss the subject. Networks, models, and information systems belong to the core.

The statement is false.

title: Two central building blocks
context: Evaluate the following statements about the central building blocks of business informatics:
statements: Understanding business informatics includes awareness of its interdisciplinarity as a central building block.
Business informatics is limited to maintaining office equipment with no link to economic questions.
The discipline is mainly a subfield of pure mathematics and knows neither businesses nor economic questions.
Business informatics covers far more topic areas than only digitization, business models, and digital networks.
The role of application and information systems forms another central building block.
tactical_explanations:
Interdisciplinarity is a central building block alongside the role of application and information systems.

The statement is true.

Maintaining office equipment without an economic link misses the discipline; it is about systems in business, administration, and the private sphere.

The statement is false.

The basis is business administration and computer science — not pure mathematics without a business link.

The statement is false.

More topic areas than the three entry fields — design, management, ethics, and systems.

The statement is true.

Application and information systems are the second central building block.

The statement is true.

title: Position between business administration and computer science
context: Evaluate the following statements about the classic classification of business informatics:
statements: In the literature, business informatics is usually positioned by its cross-disciplinary place between business administration and computer science.
The classic classification uses three overlapping areas: computer science, business administration, and business informatics.
Topics in business informatics must have something to do with computer science, and every computer-science topic must at the same time be a business-administration topic.
Depending on the focus, business informatics can be viewed as a standalone field or as a cross-disciplinary field.
In this classification it addresses questions of a business-administration and a technical nature.
tactical_explanations:
Cross-disciplinary between business administration and computer science — that is the usual positioning.

The statement is true.

Three overlapping areas illustrate interdisciplinarity and independence.

The statement is true.

Overlap does not mean compulsion: topics in business informatics need not necessarily be computer science, and computer-science topics need not necessarily be business administration.

The statement is false.

Standalone or cross-disciplinary — both are possible depending on the focus.

The statement is true.

Business-administration and technical — both natures can be addressed.

The statement is true.

title: Focus at WU Vienna
context: Evaluate the following statements about the focus of business informatics, especially at WU Vienna:
statements: At WU Vienna the business-administration focus is in the foreground and how technical aspects of computer science can support it.
Every business-informatics topic at WU Vienna must come in equal parts from all neighboring disciplines, otherwise it does not count as a subject of the field.
When classifying, a close look is needed, because depending on the focus the field can be understood as standalone or cross-disciplinary.
The classic classification by overlapping areas means that every topic must lie in all three areas at once.
Business informatics can address questions that may be of a business-administration and a technical nature without every topic covering all disciplines at once.
tactical_explanations:
Business-administration focus with technical support — typical of the WU context.

The statement is true.

Equal parts from all neighboring disciplines are not required. Focus and overlap vary.

The statement is false.

Look closely: standalone or cross-disciplinary depending on the focus.

The statement is true.

Overlap allows intersections but does not force every topic to lie in all three circles at once.

The statement is false.

Both natures are possible without full coverage of every discipline in every topic.

The statement is true.

title: Technical and behavioral perspectives
context: Evaluate the following statements about the perspectives of the interdisciplinary field of business informatics:
statements: If one expands business administration and computer science as perspectives, business informatics can be viewed from a behavioral-science and from a technical perspective.
From a technical perspective, among others production management, computer science, and data science are relevant.
From a behavioral-science perspective, among others business administration, sociology, and psychology are relevant.
Data science belongs to the behavioral-science perspective and has nothing to do with the technical perspective.
The technical and behavioral-science perspectives stand side by side and open the view onto different disciplines.
tactical_explanations:
Two angles: behavior and technology — both shape the discipline.

The statement is true.

Production management, computer science, and data science lie on the technical side.

The statement is true.

Business administration, sociology, and psychology lie on the behavioral-science side.

The statement is true.

Data science belongs to the technical perspective — not to the behavioral-science one alone.

The statement is false.

Side-by-side perspectives open the interdisciplinary field.

The statement is true.

title: Production management as a technical perspective
context: Evaluate the following statements about production management in the context of business informatics:
statements: In production management the focus is on production and the manufacture of goods and services.
Relevant topics are processes and mechanisms in production as well as managing supply chains and administering inventory and capacities.
ICT can help here to automate, optimize, and support steps.
In this framework production management belongs to the behavioral-science perspective and has nothing to do with technology.
Production management ignores supply chains, inventory, and capacities and limits itself to pure financial speculation.
tactical_explanations:
Production and manufacture — goods and services — are the focus.

The statement is true.

Processes, supply chains, inventory, and capacities are the topics named.

The statement is true.

Automate, optimize, support — ICT as a lever.

The statement is true.

Production management lies on the technical perspective, not on the behavioral-science one alone.

The statement is false.

Supply chains, inventory, and capacities belong precisely to it — financial speculation alone misses the focus.

The statement is false.

title: Computer science within business informatics
context: Evaluate the following statements about computer science as part of the technical perspective:
statements: In computer science the focus is on planning, designing, and implementing systems and technologies.
That ranges from algorithms for analyzing networks or processes to translating requirements into working software.
Topics such as software engineering, the semantic web, or complex systems appear here.
In this context computer science is limited to operating ready-made office programs; planning and designing systems are not part of it.
Hardware procurement without software development is considered the sole core of the computer-science perspective in business informatics.
tactical_explanations:
Plan, design, implement — the computer-science arc in business informatics.

The statement is true.

From algorithms to holistic system design and translating requirements.

The statement is true.

Software engineering, the semantic web, and complex systems are topics named.

The statement is true.

Operating ready-made office programs is too narrow; planning and design belong to it.

The statement is false.

Hardware purchase alone is not the core; designing and implementing systems and software count.

The statement is false.

title: Data science and large volumes of data
context: Evaluate the following statements about data science in the interdisciplinary field of business informatics:
statements: In data science, working with numbers and datasets of enormous scale is in the foreground — keyword Big Data or Open Data.
Through the use of various systems, large volumes of data arise; companies can make decisions on the basis of analysis.
Analyzing large volumes of data is trivial and poses no particular challenge.
Applications from computer science, statistics, and mathematics are combined to adapt models for forecasts and analyses.
Depending on the application area, one also comes into contact with artificial intelligence and machine learning.
tactical_explanations:
Large volumes of data and their analysis are the focus of data science.

The statement is true.

Data arises in operations; analysis can support decisions.

The statement is true.

Analyzing large volumes is precisely a challenge — not trivial.

The statement is false.

An interdisciplinary mix of methods for models and forecasts.

The statement is true.

AI and machine learning can be added depending on the area.

The statement is true.

title: Business administration in the behavioral-science perspective
context: Evaluate the following statements about business administration as a perspective of business informatics:
statements: A guiding question is how ICT can support companies in their core processes.
Advancing digital transformation and using disruptive innovations for new value creation belong to the questions.
It is also about management and how companies can comply with regulations — keyword data protection and privacy.
Digital transformation and disruptive innovations play no role in the business-administration perspective of business informatics.
The questions and topic areas of the business-administration perspective are numerous.
tactical_explanations:
Supporting core processes through ICT is the guiding question of the business-administration perspective.

The statement is true.

Transformation and disruptive innovation for value creation belong to it.

The statement is true.

Management and regulation — data protection and privacy — are part of the view.

The statement is true.

Transformation and disruptive innovations are expressly part of the business-administration perspective.

The statement is false.

Numerous questions — the range is broad.

The statement is true.

title: Sociology, psychology, and ethics
context: Evaluate the following statements about sociology and psychology in the field of business informatics:
statements: Sociology asks, among other things, about the influence of groups and organizations on system design and about effects on individuals and society.
In the usage context, the human is central: they design systems, have needs and emotions, and make ethically shaped decisions.
Psychology concerns effects of technology on people and ethical questions of system design.
Sociology mainly views systems as technical artifacts with no influence on groups, individuals, or society.
Keywords such as Digital Humanism and Ethical Computing are irrelevant for anchoring ethical values in systems.
tactical_explanations:
Groups, organizations, individuals, and society — the sociological view of systems.

The statement is true.

Humans as a central component with needs, emotions, and ethical stances.

The statement is true.

Effects on people and ethics in design — the psychological perspective.

The statement is true.

Sociology specifically brings in societal and group-dynamic effects — not only technical artifacts.

The statement is false.

Digital Humanism and Ethical Computing are keywords for ethical anchoring in systems — relevant, not irrelevant.

The statement is false.

title: Definition of business informatics
context: Evaluate the following statements about the definition of business informatics and the concept of an information system:
statements: The subject of business informatics is information systems in business, administration, and the private sphere.
The discipline deals with the development, introduction, operation, use, and replacement of information systems.
It sees itself as an interdisciplinary field based on business administration and computer science.
Information systems support companies in business-administration endeavors and are designed by people.
Information systems arise without any human design contribution; people play no role in development and use.
tactical_explanations:
Three fields: business, administration, private sphere — the subject is information systems.

The statement is true.

The life cycle from development to replacement belongs to the subject.

The statement is true.

Interdisciplinary: business administration and computer science as the basis.

The statement is true.

Support and human design belong together.

The statement is true.

People design and use systems — without them a central component is missing.

The statement is false.

title: What an application system is
context: Evaluate the following statements about the concept of an application system:
statements: An application system comprises programs as application software for a concrete business application domain.
That includes data (for example in a database) as well as IT infrastructure/hardware on which the software runs.
Application systems are developed or used for a particular company or for a particular area within the company.
Classic examples are spreadsheets with database connectivity as well as systems in accounting, HR, logistics, sales, or marketing.
Application systems are mainly developed for private household use and know no business task domains.
tactical_explanations:
Business application domain — software for concrete tasks.

The statement is true.

Software, data, and hardware together belong to the application system.

The statement is true.

Company- or area-specific — both are envisaged.

The statement is true.

Excel/Calc with a DB and business functional areas are typical examples.

The statement is true.

The business context is the core; pure household software with no business link does not match the definition.

The statement is false.

title: Adapting application systems in the enterprise
context: Evaluate the following statements about adapting application systems to the company:
statements: In the business context, procuring application systems poses the challenge of adapting systems to the company.
This adaptation can be costly and effort-intensive and is a central aspect of business informatics.
It is about translating people’s requirements so that they are implemented functionally in the application.
That requires knowledge from computer science as well as business administration or other disciplines.
For business adaptation it is enough to unpack the standard software with no knowledge of the company’s core processes.
tactical_explanations:
Adaptation to the business differs from privately buying ready-made software.

The statement is true.

The cost and effort of adaptation are a central topic of the discipline.

The statement is true.

Translating requirements — connecting people and function.

The statement is true.

Interdisciplinary knowledge secures the integration.

The statement is true.

Unpacking without process knowledge is not enough; adaptation to core processes is the challenge.

The statement is false.

title: Information system versus application system
context: Evaluate the following statements about distinguishing information systems from application systems:
statements: An information system comprises various application systems for a business context and is embedded in the organizational structure.
In contrast to an application system, an information system is an adapted, company-specific system for the organization’s special requirements.
In business informatics the information system is a central subject, because only through adaptation to organization and staff does it unfold its full effect.
Information systems are sold standardized off the shelf; consulting or internal resources for adaptation are superfluous.
An information system consists of people and machines that produce or use information and are connected by communication relationships.
tactical_explanations:
Several application systems plus embedding in the organization — the information system.

The statement is true.

Adapted specifically for the company — the difference from an application system.

The statement is true.

Adaptation to organizational and personnel conditions is what produces the effect.

The statement is true.

Often adaptation is needed — consulting or internal resources; “off the shelf without adaptation” does not hold.

The statement is false.

People and machines, information and communication — the definition of an information system.

The statement is true.

title: Components of an information system
context: Evaluate the following statements about the components of an information system:
statements: An information system is more than software; fundamentally it involves data, processes, and people.
The business uses and produces data in business cases; these can be captured in processes as work steps.
People inside or outside the company — for example customers or delivery services — process business cases and need hardware and software to do so.
Data are exchanged only locally without networks; local and global networks for communication between companies play no role.
Software can be bought standardized or adapted individually; servers and end devices support data processing.
tactical_explanations:
Data, processes, people — more than just code.

The statement is true.

Business cases generate data and are organized in processes.

The statement is true.

Internal and external roles use application systems operationally.

The statement is true.

Local and global networks are envisaged so that information can be exchanged between companies.

The statement is false.

Standard or individual, servers and mobile end devices — typical components.

The statement is true.

title: ERP systems and the SAP example
context: Evaluate the following statements about business information systems using the example of ERP and SAP:
statements: An ERP system is a business information system that, depending on the focus, supports key areas such as accounting, materials management, or production.
SAP is a German software company based in Walldorf and one of the largest software companies worldwide.
SAP has been on the market since 1972; generations range from R/3 and SAP ERP via Business Suite to S/4HANA as the current ERP solution.
SAP offers, among other things, CRM, supply-chain, and business-intelligence systems.
SAP is an Austrian hardware company with no software offering and no ERP products.
tactical_explanations:
ERP = integrated business information system across core areas.

The statement is true.

Germany, Walldorf, software group — the classification of SAP.

The statement is true.

Long market presence and several ERP generations up to S/4HANA.

The statement is true.

CRM, SCM, and BI complement the portfolio alongside ERP.

The statement is true.

SAP is a German software company with ERP products — not Austrian hardware without software.

The statement is false.
